beats.summary: Michael organizes a murder mystery dinner party game called Belles, Bourbon and Bullets for the office.

evidence.snippet: Meredith (reading the game box cover): Belles, Bourbon and Bullets, a murder mystery dinner party game.
Michael: It is so much fun. Everybody plays a character, we go around the room, we try to figure out who did it…

beats.summary: Some office members initially resist participating but are persuaded by the promise of food.

evidence.snippet: Michael: There will be food. You leave, you do not get food.

beats.summary: Characters are assigned and players begin to adopt their roles with props and accents.

evidence.snippet: Michael: OK, here are your character cards. Take one, pass it down.
Pam: I'll go. My name is Deborah U. Tante. Deb for short.

beats.summary: Andy and Erin's characters flirt and plan a date within the game.

evidence.snippet: Andy (in character): Hey there young lady.
Erin: Sounds like a plan, Sugar.

beats.summary: Angela expresses discomfort with her character, Voodoo Mama Juju, and Dwight accuses her of dark arts involvement.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: Voodoo Mama Juju, explain your dalliance with the Dark Arts.

beats.summary: Dwight accuses Phyllis, aka Beatrix Bourbon, of being the killer in the game.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Games have the power to distract people from stressful situations. Battleship got me through my parents' divorce. Operation got me through my vasectomy, i.e., my operation. I don't think I would have been able to endure my breakup
